correctness.rationale: The complete 31-choose-9 combinatorial search visits 20,160,075 subsets, finds 15,500 nontrivial blockers, and the independently described 24-element monomial stabilizer makes all the projective triangles a single orbit. The exact row reduction at nine triangle points has rank nine, so enumerating 3,906 projective quartics is exhaustive. Precisely 24 forms have no extra rational zeros; a verified free transitive action on these forms reduces geometric smoothness to one representative, whose three affine Jacobian ideals each have Groebner basis [1] in characteristic five. Thus 15,500*24=372,000 scalar classes, exactly one PGL3(F5) orbit with trivial projective stabilizer. All computations are reproducible by the two embedded complete source programs; finite rational tests are not used as proof of geometric smoothness.

value.rationale: These curves meet two independent natural sharp constraints simultaneously: the Blokhuis nine-point lower bound for nontrivial blockers and degree four, minimal by the published cubic obstruction. The complete 372000-equation classification, unique projective orbit, trivial stabilizer and exact geometric smoothness separate the result from known F5 smooth-quartic existence (whose displayed example has 11 points). This is a natural complete classification at a finite-field boundary, not an arbitrary slice or merely routine recomputation.
